title: Benchmark-delta improvement ticket and builder regression gate v0
problem: Blocked by ticket-427. The improvement loop currently turns coarse failure counts into drafts but does not require a measurable research-quality baseline, target, or before/after proof. A recursive improvement claim is not justified until ticket generation and builder completion are tied to protected benchmark deltas.
acceptance_criteria: An evaluator failure can generate a draft ticket only when it names the failing metric, baseline value, threshold or target, affected benchmark slice, reproduction command, evidence artifact, scoped modules, and safety constraints.
Ticket validation rejects vague quality tickets that lack raw counts, a reproducible benchmark, or a measurable acceptance target.
The builder gate records before and after results for the targeted metric plus all protected research, RAG, golden, and safety metrics.
A change cannot be marked successful when the target does not improve, a protected floor regresses, false acceptance increases, or required evidence is missing.
A deterministic golden scenario links run ID to metric failure to draft ticket to bounded patch/report to before/after artifact while using mock models only.
Model output cannot promote queue rows, create branches, commit, push, merge, publish, or change thresholds; existing human and autonomy-tier gates remain authoritative.
README and program report describe the result as a measured, governed improvement loop rather than autonomous recursive self-modification.
test_plan: With mock-only env: python -m pytest tests/golden -q
With mock-only env: python -m rge.cli verify
non_goals: Do not implement autonomous code generation or self-modification.
Do not permit model-authored queue promotion, merge, push, or publication.
Do not change quality thresholds from evaluator or ticket output.
Do not bypass one-ticket-per-branch or human review gates.
rollback_plan: Disable metric-driven ticket drafting and builder delta enforcement while retaining generated artifacts for audit. Restore prior governed draft flow without claiming recursive improvement.
